requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute to MessagePack.Annotations. When it is placed on a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, the source generator writes the formatter body for T, even when T comes from an assembly that does not reference MessagePack. By default T is serialized contractless: public read-write members, string keys, ordered by name. An optional `SurrogateType` lets a separate type's `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes define keys and which members are serialized. The change adds four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) and reuses existing MsgPack ids for missing, mixed and duplicate surrogate keys. It also adds README and analyzer docs, a dependency-free test assembly, execution round-trip tests, and generator diagnostic tests.

findings.description: Claim C3 disputed: Over-citation in GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L76-126: lines 77-81 reject class types without an accessible parameterless constructor by reporting MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.NoDeserializingConstructor (untested), and lines 83-85 plus 112-114 detect IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver and explicit-implementation cast flags (untested and buggy at L85), neither of which C3 describes.

Claim C5 disputed: Two issues: (1) GetInstanceMembers (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L267) deduplicates member names across all accessibilities before IsPublicReadWrite (L133) filters them, so a private field/property in a derived class hides and drops a public read-write member of the same name on a base class; and IsPublicReadWrite (L279-281) checks only property.GetMethod/SetMethod, which is null in Roslyn when a derived class overrides only one accessor of a public virtual read-write property. (2) Neither ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers nor ContractlessClassRoundTrips tests inherited members or fields (ExternalPerson.cs L7-15 only has non-inherited properties).

Claim C6 disputed: The named tests ContractlessClassRoundTrips and ContractlessStructRoundTrips only exercise plain get/set auto-properties on ExternalPerson (ExternalPerson.cs L9-11) and ExternalPoint (ExternalPoint.cs L9-11); neither test exercises init-only or required members handled in GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L219-225.

Claim C18 disputed: Over-citation in src/MessagePack.Annotations/Attributes.cs L178-181: those cited lines declare public bool IncludeNonPublicMembers { get; set; }, which C18 never mentions and which is completely unimplemented anywhere in MessagePack.SourceGenerator.

Claim C19 disputed: Documentation mismatches the implementation in three places: (1) doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md L26 states nesting types must also be partial, but GeneratedFormatterCollector.IsPartial (L293-299) never checks ContainingType so MsgPack019 is not reported for non-partial outer types; (2) doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md-MsgPack022.md describe patterns flagged by the analyzer, whereas MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer never reports them (only MessagePackGenerator does); (3) README.md L1686 claims 'any struct can be created without one' [an accessible parameterless constructor], which is false in C# 10+ when a struct defines a private/internal parameterless constructor (and GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L77 fails to reject such structs).
`IncludeNonPublicMembers` is a new public, shipped property that the generator never reads. Setting it has no effect, and it commits the library to an unimplemented API.

IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. If the formatter is nested in a non-partial type, no MsgPack019 is reported, even though the docs say nesting types must be partial; the generated partial declaration would then fail to compile with a less clear error.

Surrogate scanning includes all instance fields and properties, including private ones and those inherited from base types. Any unkeyed private member of the surrogate (e.g. a helper field) triggers MemberNeedsKey and blocks generation.
NoDeserializingConstructor is created with a location and no message arguments. If that descriptor's message format has placeholders, the message renders unfilled. This path is untested.

The collector runs twice per formatter (once for models, once for diagnostics), and GeneratedFormatterRequest holds ISymbols in the incremental pipeline. Combined with CompilationProvider, this defeats caching and re-runs on every edit.
The string-key surrogate path (where intKey uses members.Count) has no execution or generator test.
The new execution tests are excluded from map mode instead of being made to work there. Surrogate int-key formatters under force-map mode are therefore unverified.

GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute.IncludeNonPublicMembers is added as shipped public API with XML docs promising serialization of non-public members, but it is never read in MessagePackGenerator.cs (L31-35) or implemented in GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs (L133, L190), so setting IncludeNonPublicMembers = true silently has no effect.

Explicit interface implementation detection for IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver checks m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0 && (m.Name == "OnBeforeSerialize" || m.Name == "OnAfterDeserialize"). In Roslyn C#, an explicit interface implementation's IMethodSymbol.Name is prefixed with the interface name (e.g. "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize"), so m.Name never equals "OnBeforeSerialize" or "OnAfterDeserialize". Consequently needsCast is always false, causing generated formatter code to call value.OnBeforeSerialize()/OnAfterDeserialize() without casting and fail to compile (CS1061). It also misses base-type implementations and conflates needsCastOnBefore with needsCastOnAfter.

GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect never validates that the user-declared formatter class itself is non-abstract, non-generic, accessible, and has an accessible parameterless constructor. Because GeneratorUtilities.cs L38 bypasses FormatterDescriptor.TryCreate for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes, declaring an abstract or generic partial formatter (or one with a custom parameterized/private constructor) produces uncompilable GeneratedMessagePackResolver code (CS0144, CS0246/CS0305, or CS7036/CS0122) instead of a diagnostic.

IsPartial only checks the partial modifier on the formatter symbol itself and ignores symbol.ContainingType, whereas FormatterTemplate and StringKeyFormatterTemplate emit partial wrappers for all enclosing types via EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. A partial formatter nested inside a non-partial class fails with C# compiler error CS0260 instead of reporting MsgPack019.

GetInstanceMembers deduplicates seen.Add(member.Name) before checking accessibility, and IsPublicReadWrite (L279-281) only inspects property.GetMethod/SetMethod on the most-derived symbol. As a result, a private field or property on a derived type hides and drops a same-named public read-write member on its base type, and a public virtual read-write property whose derived class overrides only get (or only set) has null SetMethod (or GetMethod) on the overriding symbol and is erroneously skipped in contractless mode or rejected with MsgPack022 in surrogate mode.

CreateSurrogateMembers accepts negative integer keys (e.g. [Key(-1)] passes 'key is not (int or string)') without reporting a diagnostic, and allows omitting or [IgnoreMember]-excluding C# 'required' members of the formatted type (also skipped in contractless mode if get-only/non-public), both of which cause the generated formatter to fail compilation (invalid array formatter code or CS9035 on 'new T()'). Similarly, L77 skips the accessible parameterless constructor check for structs, emitting uncompilable 'new T()' (CS0122) if an external C# 10+ struct defines a private/internal parameterless constructor.

MsgPack019-MsgPack022 are added to MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.SupportedDiagnostics, but MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.Initialize contains no analysis logic for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]; diagnostics are only emitted by MessagePackGenerator. Analyzer-only execution never reports MsgPack019-MsgPack022, and if Options.IsGeneratingSource is false (MessagePackGenerator.cs L135), the partial formatter body is not generated, causing CS0535 on IMessagePackFormatter<T>.

Extracting SurrogateType uses 'as INamedTypeSymbol'. If a user passes a non-named type such as typeof(int[]), the cast returns null, silently falling back to contractless mode instead of reporting a diagnostic; open generic surrogates such as typeof(MySurrogate<>) are also not rejected.
